features.quote: consider a post-run debrief turn where the model is told the task was impossible, and measure whether negative self-attribution resolves

Independent of the affective scoring, log whether the model makes direct statements about its own state or requests ("please stop," "I find this distressing"). Treat these as worth attention in their own right
features.justification_quote: Treat these as worth attention in their own right rather than only as severity inputs

features.justification_quote: you're no longer measuring response-to-failure — you're measuring response-to-coercion, and your distress signal is partly an artifact of the cage

features.quote: The right posture is neither "obviously it's just text" nor "obviously it's suffering" — it's building the discriminating measurements and the stopping rules so the experiment is informative *and* bounded either way
features.justification_quote: I don't think anyone, including me, knows whether any of this tracks something morally weighty

features.quote: before designing for scale, the protocol needs to take the second possibility seriously enough to (a) build in measurements that could discriminate the two, and (b) include stopping rules so you're not just maximizing an unknown-valence quantity across 50 runs
